newsitem.title: UK: UK directors' share buying hits 5-yr peak--analyst.
newsitem.headline: UK directors' share buying hits 5-yr peak--analyst.

text.p: UK corporate directors joined in on the stock market's ebullient rise to all-time highs the last six weeks, according to a firm tracking their share activities.

Roughly four directors purchased shares in their own companies for every one selling in July, the highest ratio since August 1992 and a clearly bullish sign for the British stock market, according to Directus, a department of Edinburgh Financial Publishing.
"It's even more interesting to look at the three-month rolling average, which is very high as well and is even more significant," said Ian Forrest, senior researcher at Directus.
"I would say it's a very bullish signal," he told Reuters.
The ratio, which moved to a three-month rolling average of 3.7 to one by the end of July, was holding above four to one by late last week, Forrest said.

Asked if it might be a contrarian indicator, with the FTSE 100 at record highs above 5,000 points, he said, "When directors are buying shares in their own company, they are in the best position to see how their companies are performing."
Forrest said sterling's strength may dampen but not extinguish the impact of directors' buying this time around versus five years ago.

The FTSE 100 rose by 52 percent in the 16 months after August 1992, confirming the bullish implications of directors' buying, the group said. "The possibility of history repeating itself is intriguing," it said in a report.
The strongest sector buying in July was in building materials and merchants, printing, paper and packaging, healthcare and general retailing, Directus said.
Six directors at Seton Healthcare Group Plc bought 137,500 shares between them at 383-432p each, it said.
Four directors of packaging group Low & Bonar Plc bought 79,500 shares at 207-210 each, Directus said.
On the sell side, Moir Lockhead, deputy chairman and chief executive of FirstBus Plc, sold one million shares at 203p, cutting his holding to 1.4 million, it said.
